To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the photon energy of the radiation source influences the radiation response in MOS structures, and the interface state generation efficiency decreases as the square of the field across the oxide.
the photon energy dependence of the radiation effects is due to the electron-hole recombina-tion dynamics, and that interface state trapping efficiency decreases as the square of the electric field.

(1) The electron-hole recombination in the oxide is the dominant process in determining the flatband shift in the low field regime, and (2) the interface state generation is proportional to the square root of electric field across the Si-Si02 interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the effects of radiation on MOS structures.
the radiation induced degradation of MOS capacitors.
the effects of ionizing radiation on the electrical properties of MOS structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
radiation effects in Si-SiO 2 systems are strongly dependent on the energy of the incident radiation.
radiation induced oxide charges are not created at a uniform rate in all oxides, nor are they created at the same rate in the same oxides for different radiation energies.
the radiation-induced interface state density in MOS capacitors increases with the oxide field and decreases with the square root of field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiation induced oxide trapped charge is a function of the electric field, the oxide thickness, and the radiation source energy.
the hole capture cross section for interface traps increases with increasing oxide thickness.
the hole trapping efficiency at the Si-Si02 interface decreases as the oxide field increases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron-hole dynamics in SiO2 are important in determining radiation effects.
the photon energy dependence of the radiation effects in oxides is not a new phenomenon and that it has been observed in the past.

radiation induced charge in oxides depends on the electron-hole recombina-tion dynamics in the oxide, and the electron-hole pair production rate is not the only factor that affects the charge trapping efficiency.
